messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: adding to bayesplot histograms
parts:
Hi!

I was wondering how I can add to a mcmc_hist plot, for example, the density of a normal using stat_function. I am getting an odd error message, but when doing the plot manually things work:

small example:

x <- example_mcmc_draws()
mcmc_hist(x, pars="beta[1]")
mcmc_hist(x, pars="beta[1]") + stat_function(fun=dnorm) ## does not work
# R complains about:
# `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.
# Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'density' not found
#
xm <- data.frame(beta=as.vector(x[,1:4,3]))
ggplot(xm, aes(x=beta)) + geom_histogram(aes(y=..density..)) + stat_function(fun=dnorm, args=list(mean=0, sd=0.5))

I suppose that has to do with how things are handled internally in bayesplot, but is there a way to overlay a function? Should I open a feature request or have I overlooked something in the doc?

Thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

parts:

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: adding to bayesplot histograms
parts:
Just to have it on record for anyone coming across this post in the future (especially for anyone not familiar with ggplot2), here's why setting inherit.aes=FALSE solves the problem. In the example in question 

x <- example_mcmc_draws()
mcmc_hist(x, pars="beta[1]") + stat_function(fun=dnorm)
# Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'density' not found

mcmc_hist creates a ggplot object with a particular so-called "aesthetic mapping". In this case the (binned) value of beta[1] is mapped to 'x' (i.e., displayed on the x-axis) and the density of the points in the bin is mapped to 'y'. We don't want to use the same mapping for stat_function but, unless it is called with inherit.aes=FALSE, the aesthetic mapping used by mcmc_hist will be inherited by stat_function and result in the error above.
